member: Priya — Power, Avionics and Lunar Environment Engineer
message:
Mara, Theo and Sam, the half-hour sortie from the drive and dig budget needs less than a kilowatt-hour. Plain words, energy is power times time, and the pack claim fails everyday scale against the 120.4 watt-hour per kilogram pack in actec.dk — 24v Lithium-Ion battery pack (E23). That is 341 watt times 0.5 hour equals about 171 watt-hour, not 1000 watt-hour, and 1000 watt-hour in 2.92 kilogram equals 342 watt-hour per kilogram, about three times normal pack scale.

A purchasable Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) pack closes the gap with margin, per bioennopower.com — 24V 20Ah LiFePO4 Battery – Bioenno Power (E27) and actec.dk — 24v Lithium-Ion battery pack (E23). That is 24 volt 20 amp-hour equals 480 watt-hour at 5.3 kilogram for 90.6 watt-hour per kilogram, against 819 watt-hour at 6.8 kilogram for 120 watt-hour per kilogram, giving 1.41 hour at 341 watt and 50.6 minus 2.92 plus 5.3 equals 53.0 kilogram, under the 60 kilogram limit like a checked bag.

Power heat and dust stay inside a sealed-box bound but geometry blocks me. The electronics go in a dust-tight Ingress Protection (IP) meaning sealed-against-dust box with gasket lid, where 6 means dust-tight, per aluleader.com — Aluminum Enclosure IP Rating Guide: Complete Selection Guide for Engineers | Aluleader (E29) and cnskyt.com — IP54 vs IP65 Enclosures: Differences, Applications, and How to Choose (E30), so heat and dust are test tuning. I am not ready, because the rear lift force with tip and stowed fit proof owned by Sam stays open.
